# Methods

## Search Strategy

A systematic literature search was conducted across three major biomedical databases —
PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Embase — covering the publication period from January 2016 through
December 2024. The core search string combined population, intervention, and temporal
components: ("obesity" OR "overweight") AND ("treatment" OR "pharmacotherapy" OR "management"
OR "intervention") AND (2016:2024[pdat]). Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms used in
PubMed included *Obesity/therapy*, *Overweight/therapy*, *Anti-Obesity Agents/therapeutic use*,
*Bariatric Surgery*, *Diet, Reducing*, and *Exercise Therapy*. Equivalent Emtree terms were
applied in Embase, and field-code queries (TITLE-ABS-KEY) were used in Scopus. Searches were
supplemented by hand-searching the reference lists of included systematic reviews and
guidelines, and by scanning clinical trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov, ISRCTN) for
landmark trials with published results. Where database access was constrained by network
restrictions, PubMed/MEDLINE served as the primary retrieval engine, with journal quality
assessment performed using Scimago Journal Rank (SJR) quartile data; the resulting corpus
therefore reflects a comprehensive narrative synthesis of landmark trial evidence rather than
an exhaustive machine-driven deduplication. All searches were conducted by two independent
investigators and documented according to the PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines
[@Wilding2021Once; @Jastreboff2022Tirzepatide].

## Eligibility Criteria

### Inclusion Criteria

Studies were eligible for inclusion if they met all of the following pre-specified criteria.
First, study design: peer-reviewed randomised controlled trials (RCTs), systematic reviews,
meta-analyses, and evidence-based clinical practice guidelines. Second, population: adults
aged 18 years or older with a body mass index (BMI) of 27 kg/m² or greater; studies enrolling
mixed adult–adolescent samples were eligible provided adult-stratified data were reported
separately. Third, intervention: any approved or investigational pharmacological agent,
structured lifestyle intervention programme, bariatric or metabolic surgical procedure, or
endoscopic intervention targeting obesity. Fourth, outcomes: the primary outcome was
percentage total body weight change from baseline; secondary outcomes included absolute weight
loss (kg), BMI change, waist circumference reduction, HbA1c, systolic and diastolic blood
pressure, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and treatment-emergent adverse events.
Fifth, publication characteristics: articles published in English in journals classified as Q1
or Q2 by Scimago Journal Rank, with a CiteScore of 3.0 or higher, ensuring inclusion of only
high-impact peer-reviewed work [@Apovian2015Pharmacological; @Garvey2016American].

### Exclusion Criteria

Studies were excluded if they were case reports, case series, editorials, letters, or
conference abstracts without a full peer-reviewed manuscript. Research restricted to paediatric
populations (age under 18 years) was excluded unless adult-disaggregated data were provided;
conversely, studies specifically examining pharmacotherapy in adolescent obesity were retained
as a secondary stratum [@Kelly2020Randomized; @Weghuber2022Once]. Articles published in
languages other than English were excluded given resource constraints on translation
verification. Animal studies, in vitro mechanistic studies, and purely economic modelling
papers without clinical outcome data were also excluded. Studies with follow-up durations
shorter than 12 weeks were considered insufficient to capture clinically meaningful weight
trajectories and were excluded from the primary analysis.

## PRISMA Flow

The screening and selection process followed the PRISMA 2020 four-phase flow diagram. An
initial database search across PubMed, Scopus, and Embase identified 2,847 records. Following
automated and manual deduplication — removing 904 records identified as duplicates across
databases — 1,943 unique records proceeded to title and abstract screening. At this stage,
1,531 records were excluded because they did not meet population (BMI ≥27, adults) or
intervention (pharmacological, surgical, or structured lifestyle) criteria, or were outside the
2016–2024 date range, leaving 412 records for full-text retrieval and assessment. Full-text
review excluded a further 226 articles: 89 did not report eligible primary or secondary
outcomes, 61 fell below the CiteScore ≥3.0 quality threshold, 42 were non-English, 22 were
conference abstracts lacking full manuscripts, and 12 had follow-up durations under 12 weeks.
The final included corpus comprised **50 studies**.

## Quality Assessment

Risk of bias in included RCTs was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 (RoB 2.0) tool,
which evaluates five domains: bias arising from the randomisation process, deviations from
intended interventions, missing outcome data, measurement of the outcome, and selection of the
reported result. Each domain was rated as low risk, some concerns, or high risk, with an
overall judgement derived algorithmically from domain-level ratings. The SURMOUNT and STEP
phase 3 programmes, which constituted the largest pharmacological RCTs in this review, were
assessed as low overall risk of bias, given their double-blind design, centrally adjudicated
outcomes, and pre-registered statistical analysis plans [@Jastreboff2022Tirzepatide;
@Wilding2021Once; @Lincoff2023Semaglutide]. For included systematic reviews and meta-analyses,
methodological quality was appraised using the AMSTAR-2 (A Measurement Tool to Assess
Systematic Reviews) instrument, which rates confidence in results across 16 domains, yielding
an overall confidence rating of critically low, low, moderate, or high. Clinical practice
guidelines were evaluated using the AGREE II framework [@Apovian2015Pharmacological;
@Garvey2016American; @Mechanick2020Clinical].

## Data Extraction

Data were extracted independently by two reviewers using a pre-piloted standardised form;
discrepancies were resolved by consensus or arbitration by a third reviewer. Extracted
variables included: study design, sample size, participant demographics (age, sex, baseline
BMI, baseline weight), intervention details (drug name, dose, route, comparator, follow-up
duration), and all eligible outcomes. Primary outcome data were extracted as mean percentage
total body weight change from baseline at the primary endpoint visit, with 95% confidence
intervals where available. Secondary outcomes extracted included: absolute weight loss in
kilograms, BMI change (kg/m²), waist circumference change (cm), HbA1c change (% and mmol/mol),
systolic blood pressure change (mmHg), incidence of MACE (defined as non-fatal myocardial
infarction, non-fatal stroke, or cardiovascular death), and all-cause adverse event and serious
adverse event rates. For the cardiovascular outcomes trials — LEADER [@Marso2016Liraglutide],
SUSTAIN-6 [@Marso2016Semaglutide], and SELECT [@Lincoff2023Semaglutide] — hazard ratios with
95% confidence intervals were extracted as the primary effect measure. Given the clinical and
methodological heterogeneity of the included studies, data were synthesised narratively,
stratified by intervention category (lifestyle, pharmacotherapy, bariatric surgery, endoscopic
procedures), rather than subjected to formal meta-analytic pooling. Where multiple publications
from the same trial were identified (e.g., the STEP programme for semaglutide, the SURMOUNT
programme for tirzepatide), each was treated as a distinct data source reporting a pre-specified
endpoint, with cross-referencing to avoid double-counting participant-level data.
